correctness.rationale: For Lambda=Z^3∪(Z^3+(1/2,1/2,1/2)), the only nonzero vectors of squared norm <2 are six signed coordinate axes and eight half-diagonals. Any frame with packet radius <1/√2 has every nonempty subset sum in this 14-vector shell. An axis forces the other vectors to be opposing half-diagonals, violating independence; therefore an eligible frame is three distinct vertices of the same sign-parity half-diagonal tetrahedron (8 unordered). Their Gram diagonal 3/4 and off-diagonal −1/4 gives each permutation simplex the centroid circumball with squared radius 5/16, verified by the average-squared-distance identity. Every nonoptimal frame hence has radius ≥1/√2. For the explicit frame (−e1,−e2,(e1+e2−e3)/2), independently checked the six given centers by exact Fraction arithmetic; each permutation tetrahedron fits radius 1/√2 and pair sum −e1−e2 requires at least that radius. No lattice-frame primitivity assumption is used.
